issue.title: Go/no-go review of Footprint's own usage after the first review cycle

task_type_fields.proposal:
After the first Footprint review cycle, decide go/no-go on Footprint itself. The plan requires that Footprint pass its own test: none of its surfaces are overlay-protected. That first cycle comes once the candidate gate is met (60 days in catalog, 30 observed active days) and the `footprint.review_ready.1` notification fires.

Steps:

- Run `sase footprint show view:stats.footprint` and `sase footprint list -l hot -a everyone`, plus the `cli:footprint.*` rows.
- Decide whether the view, the review loop, and `#footprint_review` earned their keep.
- Record the decision, either as overlay keep reasons or as removal tasks.

Also reconsider the deferred non-goals that closeout phase sase-1p1.13 proposed. Revisit them only if the first review shows a concrete need, per decisions:corpus-before-mechanism:

- a sys.monitoring dark-code lens
- an offline HTML atlas
- a sase-listen monthly digest
- `share` mode with a sase.sh upload endpoint, only once outside users exist
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: This was proposed by closeout phase sase-1p1.13 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #3-#7). It cannot happen inside epic sase-1p1: it needs about two months of recorded usage after the epic lands, so it is time-gated and snoozed until the earliest possible gate date.

issue.creation_reason: The Footprint plan requires that the census pass its own test, and the land agent folded the deferred non-goal follow-ups into this single time-gated review instead of filing a wish list.
